body.statement: The algorithm \(\mathsf{Cert}_n\) terminates for every certified input. Uniformly over all experiments satisfying the declared assumptions, the reported interval obeys \(\Pr(\tau_n\in C_n)\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(n\), where infeasible budgets trigger \([-2M,2M]\). Moreover, for every \(\eta\in(0,\alpha)\) and \(s>0\), uniformly over the fixed compact profile classes, on \(G_n\) and for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(b_{\alpha}(\bar q)\le b_n+h_n\le b_{\alpha-\eta}(\bar q)+s+5\cdot2^{-n}\). The last term is the complete radius charge for replacing \(x_n\) by its directed-dyadic upper bracket \(h_n\). This covers the declared \(e_{nt}\asymp\bar q(t/n)/t\) profiles that fall outside the Lindeberg condition used for Gaussian coverage in LiZhao2026, Theorem 4(ii).
body.justification: This is the main inferential claim: computable finite-experiment validity, same-log selection safety, and profile-adaptive radius control all survive atoms.
body.gap: WaudbySmithEtAl2024 gives generic martingale validity and ChoBibautKallus2025 gives asymptotic simulation inversion, but neither gives a completed-log atomic profile certificate with oracle level and radius slack.
body.consumer: LiberaliEtAl2025's delayed-endpoint RTAR analysis can use the interval conditional on a prespecified bridge that verifies the declared moduli.
